What is CloudFormation
• 	CloudFormation is a declarative way of outlining your AWS
Infrastructure, for any resources (most of them are supported).
• 	For example, within a CloudFormation template, you say:
• 	I want a security group
• 	I want two EC2 instances using this security group
• 	I want an S3 bucket
• 	I want a load balancer (ELB) in front of these machines
• 	Then CloudFormation creates those for you, in the 	right order, with the
exact configuration 	that you specify
© Stephane Maarek
NOT FOR DISTRIBUTION © Stephane
 Maarek
 www.datacumulus.com
Benefits of AWS CloudFormation (1/2)
• 	Infrastructure as code
• 	No resources are manually created, which is excellent for control
• 	Changes to the infrastructure are reviewed through code
• 	Cost

much a stack costs you

## Orchestration versus message transport

Step Functions coordinates supported workflow steps, state transitions, retries and error paths. Queues decouple delivery; orchestration makes the stateful business sequence explicit.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

The problem is workflow coordination, not merely moving a message. Explicit states and callback patterns fit the approval sequence. External changes still need safe retry and compensation semantics.

### Avoid this trap

A workflow engine does not make every external side effect atomic. Design compensating actions, retries and idempotency according to the chosen workflow type and service integrations.

### Apply it

An approval workflow calls several services, waits for a human decision and needs auditable branching and retries. Which service should be evaluated?

**Recommended design:** Use Step Functions with a suitable callback and explicit error/retry paths.

The problem is workflow coordination, not merely moving a message. Explicit states and callback patterns fit the approval sequence. External changes still need safe retry and compensation semantics.

cards.question: When should Step Functions be evaluated instead of implementing a multi-step workflow only with queue consumers?
cards.answer: Step Functions coordinates supported workflow steps, state transitions, retries and error paths. Queues decouple delivery; orchestration makes the stateful business sequence explicit. The problem is workflow coordination, not merely moving a message. Explicit states and callback patterns fit the approval sequence. External changes still need safe retry and compensation semantics.

cards.question: What failure mode or trade-off must you avoid when designing orchestration versus message transport?
cards.answer: A workflow engine does not make every external side effect atomic. Design compensating actions, retries and idempotency according to the chosen workflow type and service integrations.

quiz.question: An approval workflow calls several services, waits for a human decision and needs auditable branching and retries. Which service should be evaluated?
options: Use Step Functions with a suitable callback and explicit error/retry paths.
Use one shared SQS message as the entire durable execution history with no state model.
Use an ALB listener rule to store the human approval state.
Use a DNS record TTL as the only workflow timer and audit mechanism.
quiz.explanation: The problem is workflow coordination, not merely moving a message. Explicit states and callback patterns fit the approval sequence. External changes still need safe retry and compensation semantics.

## Batch jobs and managed scheduling

Batch schedules finite jobs onto configured compute environments and queues. A web service scheduler maintains ongoing task capacity for request-serving applications; choose based on lifecycle and scheduling needs.

### Reasoning and trade-offs

Batch addresses finite queued compute jobs. ECR provides images, not execution scheduling. Service-style always-running capacity may waste resources when the workload consists of completed finite tasks.

### Avoid this trap

Batch is not a replacement for every low-latency always-on API. Job dependencies, retries, compute availability and cost strategy affect completion behavior.

### Apply it

A research pipeline submits thousands of independent finite container jobs and wants managed job queues plus Spot-aware compute options. Which service is a natural fit?

**Recommended design:** Evaluate AWS Batch with appropriate job definitions, queues and compute environments.
